reader.requirement: At --std 85 every level-66 RENAMES entry must stand directly after the last data description entry of the record description entry it belongs to: a 66 with no preceding record in its section, a 66 after a level-77 item, and any level 02-49 entry written after a record's RENAMES entries have begun must be refused, in every section a record may be described (file, working-storage, linkage), while any number of consecutive 66 entries after a record are legal.

The placement screens run the same code at every --std.

reader.notes: BindEntries tracks the open record and whether its 66 entries have begun; a 66 with no open non-77 record and a 02-49 entry after the 66 run are both refused with COBOL2740, and a new 01/77 or a constant entry closes the run. A 66 naming an earlier record's item is refused by the SR4 operand resolution (IsWithinRegion). Diagnostics cite 2023 text at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: BindEntries is called once per FD/SD and per section (FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs:53/156, LinkageBinder.cs:360, CommunicationSectionBinder.cs:151), so openRecord starts null at each boundary. Probes at --std 85: q2 (66 X RENAMES A as the first Linkage entry, A in the Working-Storage record just before the section header) -> COBOL2740 'follows no record description entry'; q3 (FD F2's first entry a 66 naming FD F1's item) -> COBOL2740; q1 (1985-only Communication Section: 66 after the CD's 01 record) -> exit 0, MOVE through the alias writes CSQ1 [MNOPQRSTUVWX]; q4 (SD record ending with an 88 followed by two 66 entries; WS record with an 88 then a 66; a 66 after a redefining 01) -> exit 0 [ABOK|ABOK]. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR2 the text is in SR2.
